record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Improve the comparison table for quadratic systems and piecewise linear systems with a straight line of separation, covering lower bounds or exact values for the number of limit cycles, algebraic limit cycles, non-hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles, coexistence of algebraic and non-algebraic limit cycles, and critical periods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two classes of planar differential systems:

(A) Quadratic systems: real planar polynomial vector fields $\dot x = P(x,y)$, $\dot y = Q(x,y)$ with $\max(\deg P,\deg Q)=2$.

(B) Piecewise linear systems with a straight line of separation: the plane is divided by a straight line $\Sigma$ into two half-planes $\Sigma^\pm$, and on each half-plane the vector field is a (possibly different) affine system $\dot x = a_i x + b_i y + c_i$, $\dot y = d_i x + e_i y + f_i$, $i=1,2$ (the discontinuous case, with crossing limit cycles, is allowed).

For each class, study the following quantities and provide improved lower bounds or, when possible, exact values:

1. The maximum number of limit cycles (isolated periodic orbits).
2. The maximum number of algebraic limit cycles (limit cycles contained in the zero set of a real polynomial that is invariant under the flow).
3. The maximum number of non-hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles (algebraic limit cycles $\gamma$ for which the characteristic exponent $\oint_\gamma \operatorname{div}\,dt$ equals zero).
4. Whether algebraic and non-algebraic limit cycles can coexist in a single system of the class.
5. The maximum number of critical periods of a center (i.e., the maximum number of isolated critical points of the period function of a center belonging to the class).

The currently recorded comparative bounds to be improved are: for quadratic systems, at least $4$ limit cycles, at least $1$ algebraic limit cycle, $0$ non-hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles, no known coexistence of algebraic and non-algebraic limit cycles, at least $2$ critical periods; for piecewise linear systems with one straight line of separation, at least $3$ limit cycles, at least $2$ algebraic limit cycles, at least $1$ non-hyperbolic algebraic limit cycle, no coexistence of algebraic and non-algebraic limit cycles, and the maximum number of critical periods unknown. Improve any entry in this comparison.
artifact.status_search_result: The comparison entries continue to be the subject of active research. Recent work has improved some bounds (e.g., piecewise quadratic examples with at least 16 crossing limit cycles, mixed linear-quadratic with at least 8), but exact maxima for quadratic systems' limit cycles, algebraic limit cycles, non-hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles, coexistence questions, and critical periods remain unresolved. No source establishes the exact values, so the problem stays open.

status_evidence.title: On the number of limit cycles in piecewise planar quadratic differential systems
status_evidence.snippet: Piecewise quadratic systems separated by a straight line can exhibit at least 16 crossing limit cycles, improving previous lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds for limit cycles in piecewise polynomial systems continue to be improved, indicating the comparison is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Limit cycles of piecewise differential systems formed by a linear focus or center and a quadratic weak focus or center
status_evidence.snippet: Using averaging theory up to seventh order, such piecewise systems can have 8 limit cycles.
status_evidence.claim: Research on related comparisons is ongoing, with no exact maxima established.
